plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: DE + TF activity (CollecTRI)
plan.analytical_narrative: Six aldosterone-treated vs six vehicle-treated human kidney samples, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch, unpaired. The pipeline follows the grounded procedure: sample-structure QC on variance-stabilized counts, minimal low-count pre-filter, DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization and Wald test with explicit reference level (control/vehicle) and named contrast (treated vs control), apeglm shrinkage of the reported log2 fold change, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05. Two downstream tracks consume the DE result: (1) fgsea preranked enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways as available reference collections, to give pathway-level context; (2) decoupleR univariate linear model (ulm) TF-activity inference on the CollecTRI human regulon network, run on the Wald statistic of every tested gene (not just the significant ones), which is the specific analysis the research question asks for — ranking regulators by activity score/significance and reporting the top 6 activated and top 6 repressed transcription factors driving the aldosterone response. A report step integrates DE diagnostics, enrichment, and the ranked TF list with full reproducibility metadata. Given only 6 vs 6 replicates and a single dataset, no expression-only regulatory network (e.g., ARACNe) is attempted — a prior-knowledge network (CollecTRI) is the only sound source for TF-target regulons at this sample size, per the grounded rule.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind), PCA, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Keep gene with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (6)
~condition, explicit reference level = vehicle/control, contrast treated_vs_control
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways
decoupleR ulm on CollecTRI human regulons using the Wald statistic of all tested genes
Integrated DE + enrichment + TF activity report with top 6 TFs per direction
